title: Diffusion Models
overview: Diffusion models learn to reverse a gradual noising process. Sampling starts from pure noise and denoises step by step to produce data.
objectives: Train a network to predict the added noise

method.title: Forward process
method.body: Gaussian noise is added over T steps; x_t = sqrt(a_bar) x_0 + sqrt(1 - a_bar) eps has a closed form for any t.

method.title: Training
method.body: A network, often a U-Net or transformer, takes x_t and t and predicts eps using an MSE loss.

method.title: Sampling
method.body: Starting from noise, repeatedly apply the learned denoising step to move toward the data distribution.

method.title: Guidance
method.body: Conditioning on text or classes, with classifier-free guidance, steers samples toward a prompt at the cost of diversity.

pseudocode:
t = randint(1, T); eps = randn_like(x0)
xt = sqrt(abar[t]) * x0 + sqrt(1 - abar[t]) * eps
loss = mse(model(xt, t), eps)
# sampling
x = randn(shape)
for t in reversed(range(T)): x = denoise_step(model, x, t)

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
T = 10
betas = np.linspace(1e-2, 0.3, T)
abar = np.cumprod(1 - betas)
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
x0 = np.ones(1000)
for t in (0, 4, 9):
    xt = np.sqrt(abar[t]) * x0 + np.sqrt(1 - abar[t]) * rng.normal(size=1000)
    print("t=%d signal weight %.3f, sample mean %.2f" % (t, np.sqrt(abar[t]), xt.mean()))
